text_blocks.snippet: Itching at the injection site is a common side effect of COVID-19 vaccines, and it can also be accompanied by a rash, redness, swelling, and warmth. This localized reaction is often referred to as "COVID arm". These side effects are typically harmless and temporary, often resolving within a week. Over-the-counter pain relievers and antihistamines can help manage the itching and discomfort.

list.title: COVID Arm:
list.snippet: A large, red, itchy, warm, and sometimes painful rash on the arm where the vaccine was administered is a common side effect according to MedlinePlus. This is often referred to as "COVID arm".

list.title: Other Common Side Effects:
list.snippet: Besides the injection site reaction, other common side effects can include fatigue, headache, muscle aches, chills, and fever.

list.title: Timing:
list.snippet: The injection site reaction, including itching, typically appears a few days to a week after vaccination.

list.title: Management:
list.snippet: Over-the-counter pain relievers like ibuprofen or acetaminophen, and antihistamines, can help relieve the itching and pain.

list.title: Importance of Subsequent Doses:
list.snippet: Even with a reaction to the first dose, it's important to get subsequent doses as recommended. If a reaction occurs, getting the second dose in the other arm or discussing alternative vaccines with a healthcare provider might be options says MedlinePlus.
